Synopsis:
This victim was cursed to see the future by the hag. In his initial dialogue, he is SEVERELY traumatised - sitting down, knees up, peeking out between his arms. He should sound quite disturbed, as if his sanity has long since deserted him.

He doesn't look at the player until halfway through the dialogue. When he looks up, he believes the player to be a monster of nightmares - a mindflayer. This is a terrifying moment for the player, as they are fighting a parasite in their head that will cause them to turn into a mindflayer.

In his dialogue in which he's met the player but has survived the hag, his gift is gone - but once he realises the player is the monster he saw before, he runs - terrified. 

In his post hag dialogue he is saddened and clearly traumatised by his time with the hag - and the thought of the life he could have led.

Cluster Contexts:
- HAG_HagLair_Victim_003.json: Lorin was cursed by a hag to see the future and is now a shattered, severely traumatised man—curled on the ground, rocking and muttering about corpses and ruined reflections, trying not to look at the world. The visions are violent and relentless (skull‑splitting, gut‑spilling), so he panics and barely registers anyone speaking to him at first. When he finally raises his head he mistakes the player for the nightmare he foresaw—a mind flayer—begging and scrambling away in terror. That reaction is particularly charged because the player is secretly infected by a parasitic tadpole that will transform them into a mind flayer, making Lorin’s accusation a terrifying, world‑shattering moment. In variations where the hag’s gift is gone he is still traumatised and mournful about the life he lost, and will still flee if he recognises the player as the monster.
- HAG_HagLair_Victim_003_Freed.json: This occurs if Lorin survived the fight with the hag. He is dazed and out of it. This is the victim who first say the player as a mind flayer and freaked out. 1) In scenario one, he was never summoned by the hag2) He was summoned and attacked the player and saw the player turn into a mindflayer3) He was summoned and attacked the player but never saw the player as a mind flayer
- HAG_Hag_MaskedVictim1.json: A victim of the hag, forced to wear a mask that takes away her free will so that she fights for and serves the hag. If the hag is killed, this character regains her senses and resolve. She's deeply shaken by her experience, but courageous, telling the player that she'll inform the people of Baldur's Gate of our heroism, and vowing to hunt down the hag's accomplices in the city.
- HAG_Hag_MaskedVictim2.json: A victim of the hag, bound into her service for so long that their mind is almost completely lost. This victim is wearing the Mask of Terror, which fills them with fear of everything but the hag.
- TWN_Distillery_Brewer.json: Dialog with the Brewer. He is a bloated creature who asks us to drink ourselves into oblivion with him. Player choices lead either to combat, or to the brewer drinking himself until he explodes.Twisted and creepy, a jovial barman who has been corrupted by curse to become a monstrous drunk. He speaks in fragments, swinging between melancholy, menace, and humour. Extra emphasis and derangment on bold words.

context: Lorin was cursed by a hag to see relentless, violent visions of the future; he’s a shattered man—curled on the ground, rocking and muttering about corpses and ruined reflections—and initially won’t look at anyone. The visions (skull‑splitting, gut‑spilling deaths) leave him panicked and barely able to register speech. When he finally raises his head he mistakes the player for the nightmare he foresaw—a mind flayer—and reacts with raw terror, begging, scrambling away, and screaming that the player is the monster; this moment is particularly fraught because the player is secretly infected by a parasitic tadpole that will transform them. In variations where Lorin survived the hag the prophetic gift may be gone but his trauma and mourning for the life he lost remain, and he will still flee if he recognises the player as the creature from his visions.
